reasons.A: Period diction and some mild irony, but the sentences run long and even, and the stance is more earnest and reflective than the passage's dry, whimsical asides.
reasons.B: The closest to the author's short, varied sentences with understated irony ('I have no doubt they arrived', royal neglect); it also matches his semicolon use and his whimsical deference to the Crown, though its epigrams are a little dense.
reasons.C: Good dry wit and self-deprecation ('a thing that does not often happen to me'), and its rhythm is close to the passage's, but the aphoristic punchline ending is more crafted than the author's quiet, wry close.
reasons.D: The most modern in diction and imagery ('solid with cars', 'glinting', 'made the day'); its rhythm is looser and more descriptive, and it has little of the author's ironic understatement.
